newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing output. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing output. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]

text.p: Following are a selection of analysts' comments on official data showing British manufacturing output fell 1.1 percent in May and rose 1.0 percent year-on-year.
Industrial production fell 0.1 percent on the month and dropped 0.2 percent year-on-year.

"It is often said you shouldn't read too much into one month's figures but these should not and cannot be ignore. The pound we know is too strong and is likely to head even higher. These manufacturing figures should set the alarm bells ringing. But unfortunately, I do not think they will stop the authorities raising rates. These figures highlight the problem of the consumers doing well with all the problems falling on manufacturing."
MARK BAYS, HSBC FUTURES (corrects institution from "MEES PIERSON")
"The market hasn't changed its mind about a rate rise this week. It's expecting something rather than nothing on Thursday."

"I don't think they (the Monetary Policy Committee) will respond to the manufacturing figures. They will be looking at consumer demand which is far too strong. I expect a quarter-point rate rise. The pound has come off sharply on the figures but the interest rate differential remains very attractive. Most people's expectations are that interest rates are heading higher. Compare that with the European situation where rates certainly aren't heading higher."
NEIL PARKER, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"May UK manufacturing and industrial output were both down significantly. Even though the ONS stated that there were no obvious signs that sterling strength was having an effect, we feel that this is clear evidence. What must worry is that strong consumption is leading to a rise in demand for imports, and that the trade deficit will worsen."
